close_reason: No action needed. This bead documents that the current ChatMessageEntry::plaintext / ::encrypted constructor split is correct and should be preserved — the wire-shape struct stays flat for serde while the spec invariant ('bodySnippet MUST be omitted when encrypted=true') lives in the constructor surface, with the tested guarantee that ::encrypted does not even accept a body_snippet parameter. The bead's primary value is as a tripwire for future contributors who might propose collapsing to a single bool-parameter constructor or a Builder. Keeping the bead's reasoning preserved in the close comment so it stays discoverable in bd history.
description:
Why this is correct: draft-atwood-jmap-chat-push-00 §5.2 says 'bodySnippet MUST be omitted when encrypted is true' to prevent plaintext leakage into the push payload. Most type-level approaches to this would either:
(a) Document the invariant and trust the caller (the standard 'extra: leave it to the caller' move that the rest of the crate uses), or
(b) Use a sum type (PushEntry::Plaintext { body_snippet, .. } | PushEntry::Encrypted { .. }) and pay the unification cost everywhere downstream.

The current code does neither — it keeps the flat struct shape that the wire format requires AND offers two constructors (push.rs:131-189) where the encrypted() variant simply does not accept a body_snippet parameter, making it impossible to call ChatMessageEntry::encrypted in a way that violates the invariant. The plaintext() variant accepts an Option<String> body_snippet and passes it through. The test (encrypted_entry_has_no_snippet, lines 230-251) verifies the invariant.

What a future contributor might incorrectly suggest changing:
- 'Why not just one constructor with a bool encrypted parameter?' — because then a typo could pass encrypted=true plus a body_snippet=Some(...) and the wire output would leak.
- 'Why not a Builder?' — Builder bypasses the invariant.
- 'Why not derive Default and let struct-literal construction win?' — Default would force one shape (probably encrypted=false, body_snippet=None) and would not enforce the invariant on the other shape.

The current shape is exactly the right balance: the wire-shape struct stays flat for serde compatibility, the invariant lives in the constructor surface, and both directions (plaintext-with-snippet, encrypted-without-snippet) get tested.

This is one of the cleanest applications in the crate of 'make illegal states unrepresentable, at the API boundary where it matters' — preserve it.
title: ChatMessageEntry::encrypted constructor enforces 'no body_snippet when encrypted' as type invariant
